hero.title: IGI Certification Guide: How to Read and Verify an IGI Diamond Certificate
hero.subheading: Learn what an IGI diamond certificate shows, how to verify the report number and laser inscription, and which inconsistencies require expert checks.

paragraphs: An IGI certificate can help a buyer understand whether a diamond is natural or laboratory-grown and review important characteristics such as carat weight, colour, clarity, cut, measurements, polish, symmetry and fluorescence.
However, possessing a document with an IGI logo is not enough.

The report number should be checked through IGI’s official database. The information shown online should match the physical report, and the report should match the actual diamond. Where a laser inscription is present, its number should also correspond with the report.
These checks matter because a genuine report can be paired with the wrong diamond, a document can be altered, and an inscription alone does not prove that the stone matches every grading detail.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer
quickAnswer.question: To verify an IGI diamond certificate:
attributes: Find the unique IGI report number.
Enter it into IGI’s official Verify Your Report tool.
Confirm whether the report identifies the diamond as natural or laboratory-grown.
Compare the shape, carat weight, measurements and every grade with the physical document.
Check the report date, comments and recorded inscription.
Ask a diamond professional to inspect the girdle inscription under magnification.
Match the measurements and clarity characteristics to the actual stone.
Stop the purchase if any important detail is inconsistent.
finalParagraphs: “IGI certification” is the phrase buyers commonly search for, but the formal document is an IGI grading report. IGI states that its report provides a professional opinion and is not a guarantee, appraisal or warranty.

keyTakeaways.title: Key Takeaways
items: IGI stands for the International Gemological Institute.
IGI grades both natural and laboratory-grown diamonds.
The report description must clearly identify which type of diamond was examined.
A natural-diamond report does not automatically prove the diamond’s mining country.
The report number should be checked only on IGI’s official website.
The online record, physical report and diamond should agree.
Natural-diamond laser inscriptions may be requested rather than automatically applied.
IGI states that laboratory-grown diamonds it grades receive an inscription identifying their laboratory-grown origin.
The absence of an inscription on a natural diamond does not automatically make its report false.
A matching inscription is helpful, but it is not sufficient by itself.
Carat weight and face-up measurements should be reviewed together.
Colour and clarity grades describe quality but do not guarantee beauty.
Cut, polish and symmetry are separate assessments.
Not every report format contains the same diagrams or fields.
An IGI grading report is not a retail valuation or ownership document.
It does not guarantee resale value or future price appreciation.
A report describes the diamond when it was examined; later damage or repolishing may change the stone.
Important inconsistencies require professional inspection or direct confirmation from IGI.

whatIsIgi.title: What Is IGI Certification?
introParagraphs: IGI certification is the commonly used term for the independent identification and grading of a diamond by the International Gemological Institute.

After examining the diamond, IGI issues a report containing identifying and quality information. According to IGI’s Natural Diamond Report guidance, its grading process assesses characteristics including carat weight, colour and clarity under controlled conditions.
An IGI natural-diamond report may contain:
closingParagraphs: Report formats can vary according to the diamond, service, issuing location and date. Do not assume that every IGI report must contain every possible field or diagram.

subsections.title: 1. Report Number
paragraphsBefore: The report number is the document’s primary reference.
It should appear on the physical or digital report and may also be inscribed on the diamond’s girdle. Use the number to retrieve the corresponding record through IGI’s official verification system.
Do not rely on a seller-provided screenshot when the report can be checked directly.

subsections.title: 2. Report Date
paragraphsBefore: The report date shows when IGI examined the diamond.
A report does not necessarily become invalid simply because it is old. However, a diamond may have been:
bullets: Exposed to an undisclosed treatment after grading
paragraphsAfter: Older reports should therefore receive a fresh condition and identity check.

subsections.title: 3. Description and Diamond Origin
paragraphsBefore: This field is essential.
It should identify whether the examined stone is:
paragraphsAfter: For Dalila’s natural-diamond buyers, the document must explicitly identify the diamond as natural.
“Natural” describes how the diamond formed. It does not state the country in which the diamond was mined. Geographic provenance requires separate origin and supply-chain documentation.

subsections.title: 4. Shape and Cutting Style
paragraphsBefore: This field may describe the diamond as:
bullets: Another recognised shape and cutting style
paragraphsAfter: The wording should correspond with the actual outline and facet arrangement.
Small wording differences should be assessed carefully, but a completely different shape is an immediate warning sign.

subsections.title: 5. Measurements
paragraphsBefore: Measurements help identify the diamond and explain how large it appears.
Round diamonds are normally recorded using minimum diameter, maximum diameter and depth. Fancy shapes generally show length, width and depth.
Compare the report measurements with the actual diamond using professional measuring equipment. A material difference can indicate:
paragraphsAfter: Carat weight alone is not enough because different diamonds can share the same weight while having different dimensions.

subsections.title: 6. Carat Weight
paragraphsBefore: Carat measures weight rather than visible size.

subsections.title: 7. Colour Grade
paragraphsBefore: IGI grades natural diamonds within the D-to-Z colour range under controlled viewing conditions.
D represents the highest colourless grade.
Grades progress through near-colourless and faint-colour ranges.
Z represents the end of the standard light-yellow or light-brown range.
Colour grade does not independently determine whether a diamond will appear attractive. Shape, size, fluorescence, cut, setting metal and viewing environment can influence face-up colour.

paragraphsBefore: Clarity assesses internal and surface characteristics at 10× magnification.
The grade is affected by:
paragraphsAfter: A clarity grade does not automatically tell the buyer whether the diamond is eye-clean. A professional should inspect the actual stone, especially when the report shows SI or Included clarity.

subsections.title: 9. Cut Grade
paragraphsBefore: Cut should not be confused with shape.
Shape describes the outline. Cut quality describes aspects of craftsmanship, proportions and performance.
IGI’s current diamond-grading process explains that it assesses round brilliant diamonds for cut, polish and symmetry and may provide optional cut grading for fancy-shaped diamonds.
Because IGI services and report formats evolve, read the actual field rather than assuming which grade should be present.
Do not judge fancy-shaped diamonds from the report alone.

richParagraphsAfter.value: to assess outline, spread, brightness, contrast and movement.

subsections.title: 10. Polish and Symmetry
paragraphsBefore: Polish evaluates the quality of the finished facet surfaces.
Symmetry evaluates the alignment, placement and relationship of the diamond’s facets.
These grades are important, but Excellent polish and symmetry do not independently guarantee:
paragraphsAfter: The diamond must still be viewed.

subsections.title: 11. Fluorescence
paragraphsBefore: Fluorescence describes the diamond’s reaction to ultraviolet light.
The report may state:
paragraphsAfter: Fluorescence is not automatically positive or negative. The diamond should be checked under daylight-equivalent, ordinary indoor and ultraviolet lighting when fluorescence is significant.

subsections.title: 12. Proportions, Clarity Plot and Comments
paragraphsBefore: Depending on the report format, the document may contain:
paragraphsAfter: The comments section should never be ignored. It may contain information that is not obvious from the main grade fields.

doesEveryHaveInscription.title: Does Every IGI Natural Diamond Have a Laser Inscription?
introParagraphs: No.

IGI states that laser inscription is generally applied to natural diamonds at the owner’s request. Therefore, the absence of an inscription on a natural diamond does not automatically prove that the report is false.
By contrast, IGI’s current grading-process guidance states that laboratory-grown diamonds it grades receive an inscription identifying laboratory-grown origin.
Use the IGI Laserscribe guidance to understand how report numbers and other characters can be placed on a diamond’s girdle.

expertNote.title: Expert Note
introParagraphs: One inconsistency does not always prove fraud. A girdle inscription may be difficult to locate when the diamond is dirty or mounted, and older report formats may look different from current documents.
However, explanations should be verified, not assumed.
When the report description, diamond origin, measurements, inscription or online record does not agree, the transaction should pause until IGI or an independent gemmologist resolves the discrepancy.

physicalSecurityFeatures.title: Physical IGI Report Security Features
introParagraphs: IGI states that printed grading reports use advanced security paper with at least five security features, including tear-resistant material, microprinting and a holographic feature.
Report designs can change. Therefore:
bullets: Do not authenticate a report from colour or layout alone.
Do not reject an older genuine report because it looks different from a current design.
Do not accept a document merely because it contains a hologram.
Always prioritise the official online record and physical diamond match.

isReliable.title: Is IGI Certification Reliable?
introParagraphs: An authentic IGI report provides an independent professional assessment of the examined diamond.

However, IGI’s official verification page explains that the report is an opinion and is not a guarantee, appraisal or warranty. It also acknowledges that laboratory opinions can vary according to when, how and by whom an article was examined.
A responsible buyer should therefore use the report to:
closingParagraphs: It should not be used to guarantee market value, investment performance or personal visual preference.

finalAnswer.title: Final Answer: Should You Buy an IGI-Certified Diamond?
introParagraphs: An IGI-certified natural diamond can be a suitable purchase when:
bullets: The official database confirms the report
The report identifies the stone as natural
The digital and physical records match
The measurements and identifying characteristics match the diamond
The stone performs well during visual inspection
The price reflects its complete quality
Separate origin documentation is available where required
closingParagraphs: Do not approve a diamond solely because a report number exists.
The strongest verification connects three elements:
Official IGI record → Physical report → Actual diamond
If any important detail fails to match, pause the transaction and obtain professional confirmation.

items.question: What is an IGI certificate?
items.answer: An IGI certificate is the commonly used name for an IGI grading report. It records the laboratory’s identification and assessment of a diamond’s characteristics, which may include the 4Cs, measurements, finish, fluorescence and comments.

items.question: How can I check an IGI certificate online?
items.answer: Enter the report number into IGI’s official Verify Your Report tool. Compare the retrieved information with the physical report and the actual diamond.

items.question: Does an IGI report confirm that a diamond is natural?
items.answer: The report description should state whether the examined diamond was identified as natural or laboratory-grown. Always read this field instead of relying on the seller’s description.

items.question: Does every IGI diamond have a laser inscription?
items.answer: No. IGI states that natural-diamond inscriptions may be applied at the owner’s request. Laboratory-grown diamonds graded by IGI receive an inscription identifying laboratory-grown origin under its current process.

items.question: Is a matching IGI inscription enough to verify a diamond?
items.answer: No. Also compare the official online record, shape, measurements, carat weight, clarity characteristics and natural-versus-laboratory-grown identification.

items.question: What should I do if an IGI report number produces no result?
items.answer: Check the number carefully and follow IGI’s instructions for prefixes such as J_. If the record remains unavailable, use IGI’s Missing or Problematic Report form and pause the purchase.

items.question: Does an IGI report show the diamond’s value?
items.answer: A standard IGI grading report is not a retail valuation or guarantee of price. Market value depends on the diamond, demand, supply and selling context.

items.question: Does an IGI natural-diamond report show mining origin?
items.answer: Not automatically. “Natural diamond” identifies formation origin, not the country of extraction. Mining origin requires separate provenance documentation.

items.question: Does an IGI certificate expire?
items.answer: A grading report does not normally become false simply because it is old. However, the diamond may later be damaged, repolished, recut or switched, so older reports require identity and condition checks.

items.question: Is IGI better than GIA or HRD?
items.answer: There is no universal answer for every diamond and market. IGI is widely used internationally, while GIA and HRD have their own recognition and commercial strengths. Compare them through Dalila’s dedicated certification-comparison guide.

finalTakeaway.title: Verify the Number, Match the Report, Then Inspect the Diamond
introParagraphs: An IGI report supports the purchase when the official record, physical document and actual diamond agree.
Pause the transaction whenever origin wording, measurements, inscription or online details conflict.
